notes.title: Tempest Tower is Out Now!!
notes.content:
Today is the day, Tempest Tower has officially released into Steam Early Access! Tempest Tower is an action-packed Tower Defense game with Platforming elements. You must explore, plan, and meticulously construct your base during the Build Phase. Then, execute, adapt, and ruthlessly brawl with hordes of Creepers during the Action Phase.

If that sounds like it might be for you, then check out Tempest Tower on Steam right now. If you're still on the fence then we have a demo available that you can try before you buy.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3123800/Tempest_Tower/

[h2]Introducing the HPY bundle![/h2]
Tempest Tower is Half Past Yellow's second commercial game (if you want to see some of our less commercial titles you can take a look at [url=https://halfpastyellow.itch.io/]our itch page[/url]). To celebrate this we have created a Tempest Tower x Time on Frog Island bundle, so if you haven't tried ToFI yet, then there has never been a better time to get on board! [url=https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/50600/]Check it out here[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/8984d946b930d84bc2aabe09659017b4dad1e614.png[/img]

notes.title: Take a look at Tempest Tower - Half Past Yellow's next great game!
notes.content:
Hello Sailors!

Happy New Year from the whole team at Half Past Yellow! We hope you had a good holiday break and that you’re ready for all the great games coming out in 2025 🎉
Speaking of great games coming out in 2025, check out our announcement trailer for [i]Tempest Tower[/i]! Coming soon to early access.

[previewyoutube=ik1uElp59Y0;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]Wishlist Now[/h1]
[i]Tempest Tower[/i] redefines Tower Defense with a dynamic blend of classic base-building and electrifying player-driven combat. Explore, plan, and meticulously construct your base during the Build Phase. Execute, adapt, and ruthlessly brawl with hordes of Creepers during the Action Phase. Every level is a thrilling test of strategy and skill.
We are bringing the much loved game feel and artistic charm of [i]Time on Frog Island[/i] to this next game, so even if Tower Defence isn't normally your jam, you might still enjoy this one!
If that sounds like your kind of game then give it a wishlist and follow along with the game's development.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3123800/Tempest_Tower/

[h1]Get Involved![/h1]
We are making regular updates over on the [i]Tempest Tower[/i] page, but if you want to be as close to the action as possible, I suggest joining are [url=https://hpy.lol/Discord]Discord[/url]! We have a few big things coming in the next 2 months and we can’t wait to hear what you think.

notes.title: Time on Frog Island review
notes.content: I'm not a frog, but over the past few hours I have become pleasingly frog-like. I can croak like a frog, I can perform a froggish sproing-jump, and I can even thwip my tongue out of my mouth and grab items with it, or use it as a grappling hook to pull myself up cliffs and swing myself from ledge to ledge. As a tiny human sea captain in adventure game Time on Frog Island, I've spent so much time here (on Frog Island) I've become an honorary amphibian... Read more.

notes.title: Meet The Merchant
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Meet [b]The Merchant[/b]

The Merchant has been trying to start up a basic currency on the island for what feels like far too long, but the only frog who is interested in her coins is The Carpenter, who has nothing to give The Merchant. 

Concept Art

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/4fd793a151dbe1668dfad8c6eb8e2d271b4b3408.png[/img]

She attends church sermons and frequents the tavern, but isn’t well-liked at either place as she is only there to offer her coins as donations or for trade. The Merchant is a very sociable frog, sometimes forcefully so. The only time you would see The Merchant outside of the town would be when she is heading out to speak to The Farmer, The Fisherman, or The Artist about this new cool thing called capitalism.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/14e29f287d58a02e247282dbd2687db5cfc21fca.jpg[/img]

The Merchant is wary of The Sailor at first, but her wariness very quickly turns to  intrigue in the newcomer. As an outsider, The Sailor won’t be aware of her currency’s lack of value. The Sailor is the perfect candidate to spread froge-coin.

Join the [url=https://discord.com/invite/8TkpjHHVzZ]Discord[/url]

notes.title: Meet The High Priest
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Meet [b]The High Priest[/b]

The High Priest, much like The Village Chief, is highly respected. The church is not as well attended as it used to be, but even frogs that don’t attend the priest's sermons will always stop and pay homage to The High Priest on his daily walk through town. 

Concept Art

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/031e125e82cc4014410748a6003803d284576cb5.png[/img]

The High Priest has long since left the plane of normal functioning reality, overexposure to his own hallucinogenic sweat has left The High Priest at the will of The Acolyte, simply going through the motions as he presents them. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/cb4c8fa35595a8be3ac40336fcdbd01424096125.jpg[/img]

The High Priest is exactly where he wants to be, but it would be nice to get out of the hallucinogenic trace every once in a while, the High Priest isn’t even aware that The Sailor isn’t a frog!

notes.title: Making frogs happy is a full time job in the delightful Time on Frog Island
notes.content: The original name of indie sandbox adventure Time on Frog Island was Trading Time. And after playing it, I can see why. As a tiny, gruff sea captain, I've been shipwrecked on a colorful little island after a storm, and the only way to fix my busted ship is to help out a bunch of giant frogs. If I give a frog something it wants, it'll give me something in return. It's all about trading up... Read more.

notes.title: Meet The Acolyte
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Meet [b]The Acolyte[/b]

The Acolyte is always diligent in their duties around the church, keeping his head down and taking care of The High Priest. The Acolyte's duties include: walking The High Priest around town, keeping the church clean, and ringing the church bell every hour. 

[b]Concept Art[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/6666f98ed1078998b6f96dcbfb1ef9328651539c.png[/img]

He is a bit overly protective of The High Priest, but not for the right reasons. The Acolyte is always trying to sneak small licks of The High Priest’s back, the microdosing helps them keep their confidence and vigour. Without The Acolyte, The High Priest would be lost on a different plane of existence.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/531bdaa8287035e4dba0e8ad921b5c6caa8a6e13.gif[/img]

The Acolyte is suspicious of The Sailor when he first arrives on the island. The Acolyte sees it as his job to protect the church and The High Priest, he does his best to keep The Sailor away from them.

notes.title: Meet The Hermit
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Meet [b]The Hermit![/b]

The Hermit is an old toad that lives up in the mountains above the town area. He is quite the grump, mostly because he has such a hard time sleeping at night. The church bell rings louder through the mountains than it does anywhere else on the island, because of this The Hermit has built up resentment towards the town and the church. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/5280436ef77dd2b5f1bcdc6287872212a8f7f974.gif[/img]

The Hermit is old and mostly stationary and sees The Sailor as a means to an end. There aren’t many frogs that come up into the mountains and those that do would never help him sabotage the church. Maybe he can get this strange creature to help him, after all, The Hermit is too old to climb the church tower and steal the bell by himself...

notes.title: Meet The Village Chief
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Meet [b]The Village Chief![/b]

The Village Chief is a young axolotl who has only recently taken over the “throne” from his father. It is unclear why the monarchy on the island are axolotls instead of frogs, but the role of the village chief has slowly become more and more ceremonial so the townsfolk don’t pay too much attention to the chief on a day to day basis. 

Concept Art

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/f96ee1f6040e1266b551e6f4fc63ff7efb1d705e.png[/img]

This lack of attention didn’t bother The Village Chief much when he was merely a prince, but he is often offended by the frog's indifference and lack of special treatment now that he is “in charge” making him a bit of a brat sometimes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/4fd026030a9c2d285116154b7174e5f5635a5336.gif[/img]

The Sailor’s appearance initially worries The Village Chief, the response from his guards lets him know that this creature is a potential threat and that scares him a little. The Village Chief slowly warms up to The Sailor as he sees the strange creature help out around the island. Maybe that is the best way to gain the respect of the frogs that he craves so much?

notes.title: Meet The Guard
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Meet [b]The Guard![/b]

The Guard is a fiery frog who takes her job very seriously. She diligently keeps The Village Chief safe, either by escorting him around town or standing guard by the path up to The Village Chiefs' home.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/a17490c5132c0c2b521d1214bb2dfaef014ee210.gif[/img]

The Guard is almost completely fearless, but they are shy when it comes to matters of the heart. The Short Guard has always been afraid to tell The Artist how she feels. The Short Guard wrote a love letter for her crush, all she needs now is someone willing to deliver it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/b2922168c0009d7256648a8478116a8de958645d.gif[/img]

notes.title: Meet the residents of Croak Island
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

We're very excited to start revealing more about the totally-normal native islander society of our game! Yeah no, "normal" probably isn't the right word... Regardless, as it so happens, the island that our Sailor has shipwrecked on is inhabited by a small town of large humanoid frogs! 🧍🐸! Let's start with introducing The Carpenter!

The Carpenter is tasked with creating and maintaining all the wooden structures on the island. Being the only real handyfrog available, he is always busy. Unfortunately, he is also constantly falling behind on his tasks by always misplacing the exact tool needed for the job. He could definitely use a helping hand to find them so you better keep an eye out as you explore the island!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/18da3bfedd64f509675d30e38a618ca3e865fa6c.png[/img]

Why frogs, you ask? Well, we needed some island natives and asked ourselves, "What if humans stemmed from frogs instead of apes and were left alone on an island all to themselves?" Naturally, this is it. You're looking at the first character of many in the only possible outcome of our highly scientific research and plentiful discussions on the matter.

[h1]Early Concept Art[/h1]
The Carpenter can be considered one of the simpler characters in our cast of villagers and we wanted his visual design to reflect that. Dressed in a plain vest and undersized beanie, his glassy-eyed expression almost never changes no matter the circumstance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/12229308069c301614fdcb85e578f2db70699391.png[/img]

[h1]Have you seen my tool?[/h1]
Don't let his blank gaze fool you, however! He's a master craftsman that can build almost anything and will certainly prove it to you! Just.. ah...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/34a852ca929d11daf273849d6414210be02b3081.gif[/img]

Well... He's gone and lost his tool again! Maybe we can help him find it? Oh! Is that it?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/a010bb092103661c8ec46937e8cd895b68309c7b.gif[/img]

It's a saw! Of course, it is! Obviously, you can't be a carpenter without it. Good job, everyone! Clearly, the nature of a blog means that this is almost as far from the actual gameplay as is possible but the sense of accomplishment and helpfulness is almost just as real. Trust me, though, when I say it won't always be quite so easy to find what you need strewn about the island...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/22b7948256950aac8f59081555757b0b5d58bb7f.gif[/img]

Now that he's got his saw back he can get to work! Let's leave him to it and check back later. Maybe some other townsfolk could use some help in the meantime? 

Say tuned to meet more of the Croak Island locals in future updates!

notes.title: Controlling the Sun
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Up until now, you've seen bright and sunny images of our island but what if we told you there was another side to it? Let there be... Night!

A core feature of our game is a day/night cycle that has different gameplay opportunities depending on the time of day. Not only was it important to us to have each time of day to look and feel distinct from the others, but they needed to also transition nicely from one to the next. Oh, and also you need to be able to see what you're doing when it's dark.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/jQyIrlc.gif[/img]

During normal gameplay each distinct time of day in the game lasts several minutes - so don't worry, there's plenty of time to explore and get things done while it's still light out!

What we're essentially doing is defining specific times of day and setting it up for the look we want. Then during gameplay, we interpolate between the current phase's settings and the next one based on the time in-game. We have split the day into six phases: Morning, Noon, Afternoon, Dusk, Night, and Late Night. In our case, Late Night is indefinite and doesn't need to transition into Morning otherwise it would probably make sense to also have a Dawn phase.

The settings we are defining to provide the biggest visual impact between the phases are:

[b]The Sun Light[/b]
[list]
[*] Color
[*] Direction
[/list]
[b]Fog[/b]
[list]
[*] Color
[*] Density
[/list]
[b]Post Processing[/b]
[list]
[*] Color Correction
[*] Vignette
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/49c1e259227a15f8e27770582a031560e3b0166e.png[/img]

As you can see, some settings change quite significantly from one phase to the next but it doesn't feel quite so drastic in-game since the gradual interpolation handles it all for us very nicely. Nighttime clearly stands out over the rest, and that's certainly intentional seeing as most of the time players will be out during the day and taking nightfall as a signal to rest and prepare for the next day.

That's all, folks! It's a bit of a short post this time around since there's not much more to say and the images pretty much speak for themselves. It's probably worth mentioning that configuring every setting for each phase can be very time consuming and we've spent many hours (and will probably continue spending many more!) making small adjustments here and there to ensure that everything looks right no matter the time.

As always, if you have any specific questions or comments about any of this, just pop on in to our Discord server and we'll be more than happy to oblige! With that, I'll leave you with a bonus clip of a very important nighttime activity. Good night!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/U3NErDf.gif[/img]

notes.title: Meet the Sailor
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

We hope you're having a blast [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1755950/Trading_Time_A_Croak_Tale__Prologue/]playing the prologue[/url]!

It's time to meet [b]The Sailor[/b]! The character that you will be playing as in Trading Time: A Croak Tale.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/b2bfc5b238c6161061a6372483fdabdab974a3ef.gif[/img]

While we'll still keep a lot of the narrative and background stuff under wraps at the moment (as the work is still in progress and subject to change), we'd like to showcase some of the visual aspects and early concept designs of our protagonist.

[h1]Early Concept Art[/h1]

Looking at some of our first concepts for the sailor, it's clear our lead artist, Casper, nailed down certain key elements of the character very early on.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/fa5717bbdca37a90a1c2efca17d45a7a6830259c.png[/img]

A couple of iterations later, softening the edges, tweaking the proportions, and losing the shoes, we ended up with the design we have today. It was important for us to convey the playfulness and tone of the game almost immediately with how the player character looked while still allowing for a range of expressiveness and personality when needed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/3e5a650c50525e90100d1aae6f0103d525c14484.png[/img]

Drawing a concept and designing a character is one thing but of course we had to translate it to 3D, which is often a lot easier said than done! Luckily for us, Casper was also the one responsible for doing that, so really he only had himself to blame here!

[h1]2D Inspirations in 3D[/h1]

We took a lot of inspiration from traditional 2D animation, namely playing with scaling and proportions of moving parts commonly referred to as squash and stretch. Not only did this help sell the motion of our character but it also once again reinforced our toony visuals. 

Casper had to rig and skin the character quite unconventionally to allow for this but that's a more technical post for another time!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/2af3ce6009b97f2b41267523f321b7df176c327e.gif[/img]

If you scrub through these animations frame-by-frame you can see some very questionable single-frame poses as part of the character's animation. Definitely not realistic and somewhat nightmare-inducing but when you play it back at normal speed it's all of a sudden playful and bouncy - magic!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/285eece71962d40b1ae4fb38d8feef965bf08344.gif[/img]

We're also making use of both scaling and simple 2D sprites to animate The Sailor's mouth and eyes. This gives us a lot of control over the key elements of The Sailor's face, allowing us to be very expressive and convey a lot of personality to an otherwise simple character.

[h1]The Pipe[/h1]

As an additional bonus, one morning Casper came to the rest of the team and outlined specific pipe behaviour that he claims came to him in a dream! Here at Half Past Yellow, we're all about achieving our pipe dreams so of course, we had to implement it! 

The gist of it is that the pipe looks most interesting as a silhouette in profile view instead of head-on in front of The Sailor's face or behind his head. As The Sailor moves around and rotates relative to the camera, the pipe tries its best to stay in profile as much as it can. 

It's very subtle and I'm sure it will be unnoticed by almost everyone, but now you know! It can be our shared little secret.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/bcfcf2eeafcdb807218c0c19ab65d5fda85f1d3b.gif[/img]

[h1]Moving On[/h1]

Designing a solid character visual that reacts and also controls well is truly a gift that keeps on giving and we're very happy to have put the effort in quite early in our development. Not only is it immensely satisfying to move around the world, but it is also very appealing to watch as The Sailor fluidly and without hesitation spreads mischief and creates clutter wherever they roam. 

On the other hand, we have definitely lost some (significant?) productivity aimlessly jumping around so the jury is still out on whether this has been the right move for us production-wise!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/4dd4cf10e1ff6865ebc40436e733af0cfeb148ad.gif[/img]

In any case, we're very excited and can't wait for you all to experience it for yourselves! Stay tuned for more previews and sneak peeks, and don't forget to follow us on our socials below if you haven't already!

notes.title: A Croak Tale
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41057706/64d3ecb2ccd7114b76bed5f7a9b462087515b82e.png[/img]

Just a quick heads-up... The eagle-eyed amongst you will have noticed that Trading Time has gained a subtitle and is now called "Trading Time: A Croak Tale". What's more, we've even added all-new key art showing off the Sailor and the supporting cast of frogs - we hope you like it. notes.title: Introducing Trading Time!
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

We are so excited to introduce you to Trading Time, a new puzzle exploration game from Danish developer Half Past Yellow.

When a terrible storm ravages the seas around you, casting your mighty vessel into the perilous rocks of a nearby island, you awake to find your ship in pieces, shipwrecked on a strange island filled with… frogs?

To fix your boat you will meet a cast of friendly characters, solve head-scratching puzzles, find hidden treasures, and much more as you explore the world of Trading Time. 

[u][h1]Features[/h1][/u]
[b]Explore at your own pace[/b]
[list]
[*] Make your own path in this island sandbox, you never know what will be around the next corner!
[*] Get to know the froggy locals and help out where you can.
[*] Discover new items by fishing and farming, and concoct simple brews that will change how you traverse the island.
[*] Learn from the frogs and put your new skills to the test around the island.
[/list]
[b]Trade to fix your boat[/b]
[list]
[*] Ask around for the items you need, but bear in mind that you might need to do a frog a favor to get what you want.
[*] Solve interesting puzzles to get your hands on required items.
[*] Try not to get too sidetracked by island life!
[/list]
[b]Experiment with everything![/b]
[list]
[*] Run faster, jump higher, fall slower, anything is possible if you’re holding the right item.
[*] Discover different ways to complete those crucial trades.
[*] Each object you pick up could end up being the key to something bigger.
[/list]
